messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU pool 'prod-gpu-a' CPU/GPU saturation detected. queue_depth=1243, avg_token_latency=620ms, autoscaler=throttle, action_required

alice (oncall): acked. Seeing lots of queued requests to gateway. Autoscaler reports 'scale_limit_reached'.

carlos (sre): any errors in the kernel logs or driver churn?

dina (runtime-eng): checking runtime dashboards. There's a spike in CUDA Xid entries and repeated OOMs on several nodes. Node flaps + driver restarts around 13:04 UTC. That will reduce effective GPU capacity.

beth (support): Customer impact? Any customer-facing 5xxs or slowdowns reported?

alice (oncall): Support reports escalation from a mid-market customer - timeouts and truncated responses. TL;DR: degraded across multiple routes.

eva (prodops): Autoscaler metrics: target_pool_size=120, current_pool_size=108, node_registration_lag=30s, autoscale_fail_count=8 in last 10m. Policy shows max_nodes=110 for this pool (oops).

frank (eng-manager): Wait max_nodes=110 but target 120? Who set that cap? That explains limit. Can we bump cap immediately?

dina (runtime-eng): We can increase max_nodes but with node flaps and driver churn it may not help until driver stability addressed. Suggest immediate mitigation: drain problematic nodes and divert traffic to safer pool 'prod-gpu-b' in eu-west region as fallback routing.

carlos (sre): Plan: 1) Increase pool cap from 110 -> 160 (prodops) 2) Reroute a fraction of new requests to prod-gpu-b (alice) 3) Investigate driver Xid and OOMs (dina) 4) If nodes keep flapping, enable autoscaler-backoff to avoid thrash (carlos).

eva (prodops): Increasing max_nodes now (executing terraform apply in staging then prod). ETA ~2m for control plane to accept.

alice (oncall): Implementing temporary route weight: set /v1/generate policy to route 30% to prod-gpu-b via traffic-split API. Command: `curl -X POST https://ctl.redwood.internal/route/split -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"prod-gpu-a":70,"prod-gpu-b":30}}'`

beth (support): Notifying impacted customers: sending status note to external channel with high-level details and ETA for mitigation.

dina (runtime-eng): On drivers: grabbing `dmesg` and runtime logs from affected nodes. Sample Xid traces:
```
[13:04:12] GPU0: Xid 31: Ch 0x4a pid 22345: page fault in kernel
[13:04:13] gpu_driver: oom_killer invoked on process run_infer (pid=22345)
[13:04:14] nvidia: GPU reset detected
[13:04:16] kubelet: node lost readiness -> flapped
```
These nodes are repeatedly resetting the GPU driver; each reset causes KV cache to drop and queries to spike latency.

carlos (sre): Any pattern in instance types or firmware?

dina (runtime-eng): All affected nodes are on nodepool 'nc1' with driver 535.101 and a custom kernel build 5.15. Suspect memory leak in 535 driver under heavy mem churn.

frank (eng-manager): Action item: open a hotpatch with driver downgrade or kernel tweak. Dina, can you coordinate with infra to roll a safe driver (534.xx) to the pool? Also prepare rollback plan.

dina (runtime-eng): Will do. Initiating emergency driver rollback plan: mark a canary subset of 6 nodes, deploy driver 534.86, monitor for Xid reduction for 10m, then ramp.

eva (prodops): Pool cap increased to 160 in control plane. Autoscaler accepted new limit. Current_pool_size jumping: 108 -> 116 as new nodes get provisioned.

alice (oncall): Route split applied. Early telemetry shows 18% reduction in queue depth in prod-gpu-a, overall latency down ~90ms. queue_depth=1020 now.

beth (support): External status update posted: "We're experiencing elevated latency and timeouts. We're mitigating by rerouting traffic and rolling driver patches; next update in 30 minutes."

dina (runtime-eng): Driver rollback initiated on 6 canary nodes. Logs show one node came back healthy, Xid occurrences dropped from 7/min to 0/min on that node within 3m.

carlos (sre): Good signal. Recommend fast ramp of rollback to remaining unhealthy nodes in waves of 20 to avoid capacity drop during reboots.

eva (prodops): Rolling driver to remaining nodes in 3 waves. Each wave ~20 nodes. Scheduling 45s node drain, reboot, register.

alice (oncall): Monitoring for customer errors. Support flagged a high-visibility customer still seeing failures - their traffic currently on prod-gpu-a. Beth, can you move that customer's traffic to prod-gpu-b entirely as emergency?

beth (support): Doing now. Patch applied to customer routing. Confirming on their side: they report successful responses starting now.

dina (runtime-eng): After wave 2 rollback, Xid counts across pool down 92%, OOM messages gone. Some nodes still have kernel traces from earlier flaps; those nodes in wave 3 scheduled for driver replacement next.

carlos (sre): Autoscaler thrash reduced. Set autoscaler-backoff to 60s and min_stable_nodes=80 to stop oscillations during roll.

eva (prodops): Done. Backoff active.

frank (eng-manager): Summary for postmortem: root cause = driver regression (535.x) + restrictive autoscaler cap (max_nodes 110) which together led to queue growth and customer impact. Contributing factor: node flaps amplified capacity loss.

alice (oncall): Current metrics: queue_depth=210, avg_token_latency=180ms, success_rate=99.1%. Keeping thread open for 60m to observe.

carlos (sre): Filing immediate P0 postmortem ticket and assigning to runtime + infra. Also adding short-term runbook updates: validate pool caps vs expected target before rolling new driver.

beth (support): Notifying customers that mitigation is in place and driver rollouts are ongoing; will update when fully restored.

dina (runtime-eng): Will follow up with driver vendor with repro traces and coordinate long-term kernel/driver fix.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to SEV-2. Next update in 30m unless regressions seen.

alice (oncall): thanks all. If any new flaps show up @carlos @dina please ping oncall.

frank (eng-manager): Grabbing retrospective notes. Great coordination.
